profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21711 Filigree Court, Suite C, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC1 data center at 21711 Filigree Court, Suite C, in Ashburn, Virginia, the site Equinix itself identifies as its original Ashburn facility, opened in the late 1990s. Equinix's own DC1 facility page publishes concrete numbers rather than general marketing text, 19,935 square feet of space, the smallest published footprint among the Ashburn DC-numbered buildings on this campus, paired with 2N UPS redundancy, a higher standard than the N+1 UPS Equinix lists for several sibling buildings nearby, N+1 generator redundancy rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+2 cooling redundancy, and nine compliance certifications, HECVAT, HIPAA, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC1 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates even this building. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed, including this DC1 building once Equinix arrived in the late 1990s with its first Ashburn facility. Equinix's second building, DC2, went on to earn a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth, a status this original building helped set the stage for. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and Equinix markets DC1 through DC6 and DC10 through DC12 collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the East Coast, without singling out DC1's own peering density or customer roster beyond its status as the campus's original building.

Every data center on this campus now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, that requires large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
DC1 is Equinix's original Ashburn building, opened in the late 1990s as part of the first wave that seeded Data Center Alley. It occupies 19,935 square feet and meets higher redundancy standards than several sibling buildings nearby, with 2N UPS redundancy, N+1 generator backup rated for 30 hours or more at full load, and N+2 cooling redundancy. The facility holds nine certifications including HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, and both SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and government. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC1 itself, so its absolute capacity cannot be stated from the operator's published specifications.

DC1 sits within Equinix's 15-facility Ashburn campus spanning two jurisdictions, a cluster whose combined power draw is not published. Ashburn's Data Center Alley region as a whole represents roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power across all operators. The Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, a status DC1 helped establish when it opened alongside DC2, which Data Center Dynamics credits as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Virginia's State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 requiring large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts effective January 1, 2027, locking in long term electricity costs for the region's largest data center operator.

Across Virginia, 330 facilities are mapped, but only 25 publish power capacity. Of those 25, this campus ranks 26th by published megawatts, placing it outside the state's top tier by the single metric the operator discloses. The state's published capacity totals 1,603.4 megawatts, nearly all of it concentrated in Northern Virginia's data center cluster, but DC1's individual contribution to that figure is not published and therefore cannot be assessed from the operator's specifications alone.
